title: A common positive-degree central element
statement:
Let $\mathcal F^{(1)}_0,\ldots,\mathcal F^{(a)}_0$ be lisse
Weil sheaves on the same normal geometrically connected curve
whose Weil representations are semisimple
([def-wf-semisimple-module]; such sheaves are geometrically semisimple
by [lem-mg-normal-restriction-semisimple]),
and let $\rho=\bigoplus_i\rho_i$. There are an integer $m>0$ and

$$
z\in Z\bigl(G_{\mathrm{arith}}(\rho)\bigr)\cap G^{[m]}.
$$

Thus all Weil subquotients of all the $\mathcal F^{(i)}_0$ may be
measured using images of one and the same degree-$m$ element, via the
functoriality of [lem-mg-degree-component-functoriality].

proof.text: Put $K=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ and let $V_i$ be the stalk representation of $\mathcal F^{(i)}_0$ as in [def-wf-fundamental-representation]. All representations act through the same Weil group. Write each semisimple $V_i$ as a direct sum $\bigoplus_{j\in J_i}S_{ij}$ of simple Weil modules, using [def-wf-semisimple-module]. Then $V=\bigoplus_iV_i=\bigoplus_{(i,j)}S_{ij}$ is itself semisimple: the action is componentwise and the displayed summands are the same simple modules. The empty family gives the zero module, the empty direct sum, so it is included. Choose a basis of the finite-dimensional $V$. The degree datum and this matrix representation are the represented datum of [d-monodromy], with $F=\rho(s)$ and $H=H_{\mathrm{geom}}$. In particular $H\subseteq G_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ and $F\in G_{\mathrm{Zar}}$. The coefficient field $K$ is algebraically closed of characteristic zero, so the coefficient hypotheses needed in the next step hold.

source.place: first paragraph: the direct sum is a semisimple represented degree datum

proof.text: Apply [p-central] to this semisimple represented degree datum over $K$. In the notation of [d-central], obtain $N>0$ and $z_{\mathrm{mat}}\in Z(G_{\mathrm{Zar}})(K)\cap H(K)F^N$. Unpack membership in the translate to choose $h\in H(K)$ with $z_{\mathrm{mat}}=hF^N$. Set $m=N$ and $z=(h,N)$. By [def-wf-degree-components] this is an element of $G^{[N]}$ in the arithmetic extension of [def-wf-arithmetic-monodromy-extension].

source.place: first paragraph: apply p-central; second paragraph: put m=N and z=(h,m)

proof.text:
Use the multiplication in [def-wf-arithmetic-monodromy-extension], with $\alpha(x)=FxF^{-1}$. Since $F\in G_{\mathrm{Zar}}$, centrality of $hF^N$ gives $hF^NF=FhF^N$. Commute the two powers of $F$ and cancel $F^N$ on the right to obtain $hF=Fh$. Thus $F^nhF^{-n}=h$ for every $n\in\mathbf Z$ (including negative $n$, by taking inverses in the commutation equality). For any $x\in H(K)\subseteq G_{\mathrm{Zar}}(K)$, centrality also gives $hF^Nx=xhF^N$, hence $hF^NxF^{-N}=xh$. Therefore, for every $(x,n)$ in the extension,
$$z(x,n)=(hF^NxF^{-N},N+n)=(xh,N+n),$$
$$ (x,n)z=(xF^nhF^{-n},n+N)=(xh,n+N).$$
The coordinates agree since $N+n=n+N$. Thus $z$ commutes with every element and lies in $Z(G_{\mathrm{arith}}(\rho))$. This calculation uses no injectivity of the matrix map across different degrees.

source.place: second paragraph: lift centrality from the matrix to the degree-graded extension

proof.text: The parenthetical geometric semisimplicity of each given sheaf follows directly from [lem-mg-normal-restriction-semisimple], applied to its finite-dimensional semisimple Weil representation and the normal geometric subgroup, which is the kernel of the degree map in [d-monodromy]. For any Weil-stable subquotient $Q$ of a $V_i$, the inclusion of the direct summand $V_i\subseteq V$ exhibits $Q$ as a Weil-stable subquotient of $V$ as well. Apply [lem-mg-degree-component-functoriality] to this $Q$ and the monodromy data of [def-wf-monodromy-data]. Its homomorphism $\Phi_Q$ preserves degree and sends central elements to central elements; consequently $\Phi_Q(z)$ is central of the same positive degree $N$. The single $z$ chosen before $Q$ therefore works simultaneously for every such subquotient.

source.place: last sentence: the same positive degree central element measures every subquotient

proof_origin.place: Both paragraphs; semidirect-product centrality expanded by the coordinate calculation of Monodromy.lean:1062–1093.
